open_points.subject: AuditRecord creation for significant operations that fail on Registry or storage
open_points.text: State 0 says, “an operation that fails on storage or the Registry before that is not recorded (R0-25),” while M36 says, “every significant action — an action of the closed audit action catalog (State 2) — writes exactly one record” and defines rejected audit records for significant mutations.
open_points.question: When a catalogued significant operation fails because Registry or storage fails before the business operation completes, is no AuditRecord created, or must exactly one rejected AuditRecord be created?
options: Create no AuditRecord for any such pre-completion Registry or storage failure.
Create one rejected AuditRecord because the requested operation is a significant catalogued action.
Apply the no-record exception only to snapshot import, despite the new sentence saying “an operation.”
open_points.default_guess: Create no AuditRecord, treating the new State 0 timing rule as an explicit exception to M36.

witness.initial: An active operator has an active assignment to an active project containing an existing expense; audit persistence is available, but Registry validation times out.
events: The operator submits a correction to the expense.
The portal reaches the Registry check and receives a timeout before completing the correction.
outcomes: No AuditRecord is written because the operation failed on Registry before completion.
One rejected expense-correction AuditRecord is written because expense correction is a significant catalogued action and M36 requires exactly one record.
witness.observer: An administrator or auditor inspecting the audit history.
